nodes.summary: Let $c$ be an element of a linearly ordered type and $L$ a list over it, and let $(m, r)$ be the pair returned by minimum extraction from $L$ with initial candidate $c$. Then the list $m$ followed by $r$ is a permutation of the list $c$ followed by $L$, $m \le c$, and $m \le x$ for every element $x$ of $L$.
nodes.title: Correctness of minimum extraction

nodes.summary: For every element $c$ of a linearly ordered type and every list $L$ over it, minimum extraction from $L$ with initial candidate $c$ has cost exactly $|L|$, the length of $L$; that is, it performs exactly $|L|$ order comparisons.
nodes.title: Cost of minimum extraction

nodes.summary: Given an initial candidate $c$ in a linearly ordered type and a list $L$, minimum extraction returns a pair $(m, r)$ together with a cost. If $L$ is empty, it returns $c$ with the empty list at cost $0$. If $L$ has head $x$ and tail $L'$, it compares $x$ with $c$ at cost one: if $x < c$, it extracts from $L'$ with candidate $x$, obtaining $(m, r)$, and returns $m$ with the list $c$ followed by $r$; otherwise it…
nodes.title: Minimum extraction

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ over a linearly ordered type, the list returned by selection sort on $L$ is sorted in nondecreasing order (each entry is $\le$ every later entry) and is a permutation of $L$, so it preserves duplicate multiplicities.
nodes.title: Correctness of selection sort

nodes.summary: For every list of length $n$ over a linearly ordered type, selection sort has cost exactly $n(n-1)/2$ in the model that charges one unit per order comparison; that is, it performs exactly $n(n-1)/2$ comparisons.
nodes.title: Comparison count of selection sort

nodes.summary: Selection sort of a list $L$ over a linearly ordered type is defined recursively. If $L$ is empty, the result is the empty list at cost $0$. If $L$ has head $x$ and tail $L'$, minimum extraction from $L'$ with initial candidate $x$ yields a minimum $m$ and the list $r$ of remaining elements, and the result is $m$ followed by the selection sort of $r$. The cost is the sum of the costs of all these minimum extractions.
nodes.title: Selection sort

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
